title: Experimental and Theoretical Study of Energy Transfer Processes in Fiber-Optic Functional Systems with a GaAs-Based Photodiode Converter
content: A comprehensive experimental-theoretical study of a fiber-optic control and measurement system for simultaneous remote transmission of energy flows and information based on conversion of laser radiation into electrical energy using a gallium arsenide (GaAs) photoelectric converter is presented. The purpose of the study is to establish the effects of the wavelength of radiation, the geometric parameters of the optical fiber and the tem-perature regime of the converter on the energy characteristics of the system, as well as to develop a conceptual and theoretical generalized nonlinear physical and mathematical model of interconnected electrodynamic, kinetic and thermal processes in functional elements based on dielectric waveguides. The theoretical part of the study provides a conjugate description of the electromagnetic field, carrier transfer, relaxation polarization and heat transfer, based on Maxwell's equations, a generalized kinetic equation and a non-linear equation of thermal conductivity. The proposed closed system of equations (energy, material) of the model is generalized and requires, in the future, more specific (taking into account the specifics of physical processes in an optical fiber sample in an electromagnetic wave field) theoretical and numerical studies of the electrophysical and optical properties of materials of this class in a wide range of field parameters and temperatures (by comparing the results of theory and experiment). Six energy channel configurations were experimentally studied, formed by combinations of wavelengths of 650 and 850 nm and nominal fiber core diameters (9, 50 and 62.5 microns). The output electrical characteristics of the GaAs converter, the maximum load power and the tem-perature dependence of the normalized energy indicator are determined. The highest power output was 0.179 W at 850 nm and 0.146 W at 650 nm for a fiber with a core of 62.5 μm; the corresponding values of the energy indicator reached 0.559 and 0.456 (a de-crease in this indicator was established when the converter was heated). Experimentally confirmed the possibility of simultaneous transmission of energy and information on physically separate optical fibers. The results justify the need for a comprehensive consideration of optical losses, fiber geometry, photovoltaic converter characteristics and thermal conditions when designing remote optical power supply systems.
